Craftsman walk-up in Capitol Hill with vibrant city views, this 1968 residence has been extensively remodeled with a clear respect for its architectural roots. Vaulted ceilings, skylights, and expansive windows create a constant dialogue between interior and landscape, while stone fireplaces and a flagstone foyer ground the home in its era. The scale is generous but considered—4 bedrooms, 2.75 baths, with three bedrooms, including a true primary suite, on the main floor, plus a non-conforming 5th bedroom and large, finished space for creative and physical flexing—or more space for all the things. Two bars, because one isn’t enough, and a well-appointed walk-in pantry with abundant storage make entertaining effortless. At the center of it all are the vibrant city views, enjoyed from both upper and lower living spaces. An indoor cedar sauna adds a separate layer of retreat and restoration. The kitchen and dining connect seamlessly to the Trex deck, with a lower patio and private fenced backyard extending the outdoor experience. All systems updated: roof, electrical, HVAC, plumbing—so you won’t be spending your weekends solving problems. 2 car garage, AC, custom window treatments, the list goes on. Moments from Cal Anderson Park, Pike and Pine, indie music venues, and dive bars beside cocktail rooms, with easy access to the light rail station to SeaTac—everyday convenience, just down the street. A true Craftsman that holds its ground.
